title: Canticle of the Creatures (1225)
hookLine: tradition says he was nearly blind when he sang of brother sun, sister water, and at the end sister death

lines: A SICK MAN SINGS OF THE SUN.
cards: Laudato si', mi' Signore. Four words in the old Italian of Umbria, the everyday speech of Assisi, not the Latin of the Church: praised be you, my Lord.

Tradition says Francis made the song that starts with them near the end of his life, sick, his eyes in pain, unable to bear the light, lying in a small hut near San Damiano, where Clare and her sisters lived.
A man who could barely look at the sun named it first among the creatures. And he wanted his brothers to sing it out loud as they went about. Its first creature: Brother Sun.

teach.b: The canticle walks through creation and names everything like a relative. Brother sun, who brings the day, beautiful and radiant. Sister moon and the stars, bright and precious.
Brother wind, and air, and every kind of weather. Sister water, which the song calls useful, humble, precious and pure. Brother fire, who lights the night, playful and strong.
And our sister, mother earth, who feeds us and brings out fruit and colored flowers and grass. Nothing in it is just a thing. Everything is kin.
Tradition says a verse was added when the bishop and the mayor of Assisi were feuding: praise for those who forgive for love, and bear sickness and trouble in peace.
The brothers sang it in front of both men, the story goes, and the quarrel ended.
Near the very end comes a line that is hard to sing lightly: praised be you, my Lord, for our sister bodily death, from whom no one living can escape.

teach.h: THE PSALM'S OLD CALL, MADE FAMILY.
teach.b: Not an enemy. Not a thief in the night.
A sister. Tradition says Francis added it when he knew he was dying, and asked his brothers to sing the canticle to him.
The song sits beside the psalms the Church already sang: in the Douay-Rheims, Psalm 148 calls on sun and moon and stars, fire and hail, snow and ice, mountains and beasts, to praise the Lord.
Francis took that old call and made it a family, right down to sister death.

how: Franciscans sing and pray the Canticle of the Creatures, sometimes called the Canticle of Brother Sun, and its opening words gave the title to a papal letter on care for creation, Laudato si'.

o: a nickname for Francis among his brothers
Francis's name for the sun in his song of praise
a friar who rang the morning bell at dawn

games.q: the canticle's family — tap the pairs.

s: Francis wrote the canticle in Latin
he wrote it in the old Italian of Umbria, the speech of Assisi.
the canticle calls death a sister
near the end it names our sister bodily death, from whom no one living can escape.
the canticle ends with the sun
brother sun comes early; the peacemakers and sister death come near the end.

games.q: you're Francis. the bishop and the mayor of your town are feuding. what do you do?
o: write each of them a sharp letter.
add a verse to your song about forgiveness, and have the brothers sing it in front of both.
games.why: tradition says he added the verse about those who forgive for love, and the quarrel ended when the brothers sang it.

practice: Pick one element close to you right now, the water in a glass, the light through a window, the air going in and out of you, and give it its name the way the canticle does: brother, sister. Attend to how quietly it does its work.
If you pray, borrow Francis's opening, praised be you, my Lord; if you don't, let gratitude be enough.

wordCard.voice: Brother Sun. The first creature Francis named in his canticle, praising God through sun and moon, wind and water, fire and earth, down to sister death. Today's word.

orig.note: Old Umbrian Italian, not Church Latin: praised be you, my Lord. The canticle's repeated opening.

carryVoice: Your line: sister death. In the canticle, even the end is family. See you tomorrow.

sources.ref: Francis of Assisi, Canticle of the Creatures
